title: Chen in Claude Code
goal: Chen uses Claude Code in the same project. The plugin gives Claude the same recall, and the same propose path with the permission dialog of Claude Code as the confirmation.
place: Chen's checkout `~/example-project`. The kit is in `~/tenant-pi`.

steps.title: Chen starts Claude Code with the plugin
before: The plugin must load in place, because it imports the core of the kit by a relative path. The option `--plugin-dir` does that.
Chen ran the two `npm ci` commands of the plugin README once before.
after: Claude Code loads a recall hook and an MCP server with five tools.

steps.title: What the hook returns
before: Claude Code runs the hook for each prompt. It gives the hook the prompt, the session id and the working directory on standard input.
Chen can run the hook by hand. This sends the prompt to AWS, as a real prompt does.

frame.title: chen@laptop: ~/example-project
frame.source: `packages/agentcore-claude/scripts/recall.mjs` and `src/hook.mjs` of the plugin, with the core and a fake client

lines.text: printf '%s' '{"prompt":"Which port does the API use in development?","session_id":"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004","cwd":"/home/chen/example-project"}' | node ~/tenant-pi/packages/agentcore-claude/scripts/recall.mjs

after: The hook prints one JSON object. `additionalContext` holds the same block as in Pi, with Chen's recall set.
On any failure the hook prints `{}` and exits with 0, so the prompt goes on without context.

steps.title: Chen asks a question
before: Chen types a question in Claude Code.

after: Chen has no private record yet, so the block holds no line from `/actor/chen/`.

steps.title: Chen asks to propose
before: The description of the tool `memory_propose` tells the agent to show the exact text and the target project first, and to ask.

steps.title: The permission dialog
before: Claude Code shows its permission dialog with the tool input.
The tool carries the flag `anthropic/requiresUserInteraction`. So the dialog comes on every call, also in the modes that skip other dialogs, and an allow rule does not skip it.

frame.title: claude: ~/example-project
frame.source: the permission dialog as `packages/agentcore-claude/README.md` describes it; the look is drawn, not recorded

lines.title: Tool use
lines.text:
agentcore-memory - memory_propose(text: "The API of example-project returns dates in UTC.") (MCP)
Propose a record to the shared project memory

Do you want to proceed?
options: 2. No, and tell Claude what to do differently (esc)

after: Chen chooses Yes. The server then checks that the core writes exactly the text and the project of the dialog.

steps.title: The record id
before: Without a `projectId`, the server resolves the project from its working directory.

after: The record is in `/project/example-project/proposals/chen/`. Its metadata says `claude-code` as `agent` and `harness`.

steps.title: Chen cannot review
before: The plugin also has the four review tools of a maintainer. Chen is a member only. The two read tools follow the normal permission rules of Claude Code.

frame.title: claude: ~/example-project
frame.source: the tools of `packages/agentcore-claude/src/server.mjs` with the core and a fake client; the Claude Code screen follows the plugin README, not a recorded session

lines.text: List the open proposals of Dana in example-project.
You are not a maintainer of example-project, so the memory refuses the list.

after: The core refuses with the fixed code `not_maintainer` before any AWS call. IAM would deny the call too.

learned: The plugin gives Claude Code the same recall and propose as Pi, through one core.
The hook prints the context block as `additionalContext`, or `{}` on any failure.
The permission dialog of Claude Code is the confirmation of a proposal.
A tool refusal is one fixed code, for example `not_maintainer`.
cannot: The hook cannot write a record. It calls recall only.
A slash command, an empty prompt or a prompt of fewer than three characters sends no query.
A failure of AWS cannot block the prompt.
An allow rule cannot skip the dialog of `memory_propose`. The plugin ships no allow entry.
Chen cannot list, approve or reject the proposals of `example-project`.
notVerified: The plugin in a live Claude Code session. The live proof ran Pi and the core CLI only.
The look of the permission dialog and of the tool lines on the Claude Code version that a person runs.
The forced dialog in the `acceptEdits`, `auto` and `bypassPermissions` modes. The Claude Code documentation states it.
Whether the chat of Claude Code shows the hook context.
The working directory of the MCP server process. The project resolution without `projectId` depends on it.
